sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Agrarian Base**: The economy relied on **wet cultivation** (paddy) and **dry cultivation** (millets/cotton). State revenue was primarily derived from land tax, typically **1/6th** of the produce.
• **Monetization**: High circulation of gold coins, notably the **Varaha** (also called Pagoda or Pon), which served as the standard currency for international trade.
• **Nayankara System**: A quasi-feudal military-administrative arrangement where **Nayakas** (military chiefs) were granted land (Amaram) in exchange for maintaining troops and paying tribute to the King.
• **Key Metric**: The **Ayagar System** functioned as the village-level administrative unit, consisting of 12 hereditary officials who managed local production and tax collection.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Irrigation Infrastructure**: Massive investment in tanks (Kere) and canals (e.g., Tungabhadra river diversion) to boost agricultural surplus.
• **Urbanization**: Development of 'Pettas' (market towns) around temples, which acted as centers of economic redistribution.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Over-reliance on Nayakas led to centrifugal tendencies; high taxation on artisans and peasants caused occasional revolts.
• **Solutions**: Centralized oversight by the 'Rayasam' (secretariat) and strategic control of trade routes.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'V-A-N' (Varaha, Ayagar, Nayankara).
• **Decoded Meaning**: V = Currency (Varaha), A = Village Admin (Ayagar), N = Military Admin (Nayankara).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse 'Nayankara' (military-feudal) with 'Ayagar' (village-administrative). Nayakas were often outsiders/military commanders, while Ayagars were local hereditary officials.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Temple-Urbanization' to explain how temples acted as banks, employers, and centers of economic activity in the Vijayanagar Empire.

keyTakeaways: The economy was a blend of centralized fiscal control and decentralized military-administrative delegation.
The Ayagar system provided the stability required for agrarian taxation, while the Nayankara system provided the military muscle.
Maritime trade and the gold Varaha coin integrated the empire into the global Indian Ocean trade network.
